description.value: A 30-site provincial campground in Naikoon Park on Haida Gwaii, set among a hundred kilometres of wild beach of deep Haida cultural significance; the park is a true wilderness with no supplies, cash-only payment, and cool foggy winds possible any day of the year.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The primary evidence is the BC Parks Naikoon Park webpage, which explicitly names Misty Meadows campground and states 'There is no internet access at Misty Meadows campground or Agate Beach campground' (corroborating OSM internet_access=no) and 'Only cash payments are accepted at the campgrounds.' The website also warns visitors that Naikoon Park 'is a wilderness area with no supplies of any kind. Accommodation in nearby communities is limited,' providing direct negative evidence for food availability nearby. OSM confirms a 30-site campground with a fee, operated by the Old Massett Village Council; the website URL matches the OSM-provided URL confirming it is current.
concerns: The OSM phone number (+1 250-626-3337) and email (omvcadmin@mhtv.ca) belong to the park operator (Old Massett Village Council), not BC Parks; the website does not list or corroborate this specific phone number.
The linked website (bcparks.ca/naikoon-park/) is the general Naikoon Park page, not a dedicated Misty Meadows campground page; no more specific URL is available in OSM or on the site.
No civic address is provided in OSM.
Website explicitly states only cash payments are accepted at the campgrounds; cyclists without cash would be unable to pay on arrival.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Misty Meadows is a legitimate, active provincial campground serving one of BC's most remote and scenic cycling destinations on Haida Gwaii; it is a meaningful and likely essential overnight stop for cyclists touring the region.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website confirms no internet access specifically at Misty Meadows campground and cash-only payment. The wilderness advisory ('no supplies of any kind') means cyclists must carry all food, fuel, and supplies before entering the park.
